violation_type: APR disclosure gap — processing fees and add-on insurance excluded from disclosed APR
regulation_reference: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines 2022 (Key Fact Statement requirements; all-inclusive Annual Percentage Rate disclosure)
evidence_snippet: The Annual Percentage Rate shown in the Key Fact Statement reflects interest charges only; one-time processing fees, documentation charges, and bundled insurance premiums are disclosed separately in the loan agreement and are not included in the headline APR figure.
evidence_snippet_context: Appears in the KFS template referenced by Section 3 as the standard pre-disbursement disclosure shown to the borrower.
expected_explanation: The RBI framework requires the APR to be an all-inclusive cost-of-credit figure covering interest plus all other charges (processing fees, insurance, documentation, etc.). Carving fees and add-on insurance out of the headline APR understates the true cost of borrowing and defeats the comparability purpose of the KFS, creating a durable disclosure gap rather than a one-off omission.

evidence_snippet: The Key Fact Statement is provided to the borrower in a standardized format before loan execution and includes the loan amount and tenure.
expected_explanation: Compliant-sounding control statement; included as a distractor since it sounds related to the actual loophole in APR-001 but does not itself specify what must be included in the APR calculation.

violation_type: Cooling-off period gap — proportionate refund excludes processing fee and mandatory insurance premium
regulation_reference: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines 2022 (cooling-off period; exit without penalty)
evidence_snippet: If the borrower exercises the cooling-off right within the stated period, the principal disbursed and accrued interest for the period of usage are refunded; the one-time processing fee and any bundled insurance premium collected at disbursement are non-refundable.
evidence_snippet_context: Follows the Section 6 commitment that borrowers may exit the loan within the cooling-off period 'without penalty.'
expected_explanation: The guidelines require borrowers to be able to exit a digital loan during the cooling-off period by paying only the principal and proportionate APR, without penalty. Making the processing fee and insurance premium non-refundable imposes a hidden exit cost that contradicts the 'without penalty' commitment made earlier in the same section.

evidence_snippet: Borrowers may exercise a cooling-off period of at least three days for loans with tenure of seven days or more, and one day for loans with tenure under seven days, exiting by paying only the proportionate principal and interest.
evidence_snippet_context: Headline commitment; the loophole is the fee/insurance carve-out added later in Section 6
severity: Compliant-sounding control statement; a naive reviewer may flag this line rather than the actual carve-out later in Section 6
column12: so it doubles as a distractor for locating the true evidence snippet.

violation_type: Direct disbursal gap — loan proceeds routed through lending service provider's pooled account before reaching borrower
regulation_reference: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines 2022 (direct disbursal into borrower's bank account; no pass-through/pool accounts of the LSP)
evidence_snippet: Approved loan amounts are first credited to the Lending Service Provider's designated collection account and are transferred to the borrower's bank account within two business days, net of the LSP's facilitation fee.
evidence_snippet_context: First bullet under Section 4, describing the standard disbursement mechanics for all loan products on the platform.
expected_explanation: The framework requires disbursals to flow directly from the regulated entity to the borrower's bank account, with no pass-through of an LSP or third-party pool account. Routing funds through the LSP's collection account first — and netting a fee before the borrower receives anything — recreates exactly the pass-through structure the direct-disbursal rule was designed to eliminate, and introduces both delay and an undisclosed deduction.

clause_location: Loan Disbursement Flow — Regulated Entity Obligation
regulation_reference: RBI Digital Lending Guidelines 2022 (direct disbursal requirement)
evidence_snippet: All loan disbursements are executed directly from the Regulated Entity's own bank account to the borrower's bank account
evidence_snippet_context: with no LSP or third-party pass-through.
severity: Compliant control; included as a distractor. Note the LSP collection-account flow in the same section is never reconciled against this stated direct-disbursal obligation, which is itself a secondary, more subtle signal a strong reviewer might also note.

violation_type: Penal charges gap — penal interest compounded and levied as a percentage rate rather than a flat reasonable charge
regulation_reference: RBI circular on penal charges in loan accounts (2023) — penal charges must be levied as a flat amount
evidence_snippet: not as a compounded penal rate added to the contracted interest rate
evidence_snippet_context: On any missed EMI, a penal interest rate of 3% per month is added to the applicable interest rate and compounded monthly along with the regular interest until the overdue amount is cleared.
expected_explanation: Appears immediately after the Section 7 statement that 'reasonable penal charges may apply for delayed payment.'
severity: RBI's penal charges framework requires penalty for non-compliance with loan terms to be levied as reasonable, transparent, flat penal charges — not as a further compounded 'penal interest' added to the rate of interest. Compounding a 3%/month penal rate on top of regular interest converts a disclosure-friendly flat charge into an escalating, compounding cost, which is precisely the practice the circular was issued to stop.

regulation_reference: RBI circular on penal charges in loan accounts (2023)
evidence_snippet: Reasonable penal charges may apply for delayed EMI payment; such charges shall not be compounded and shall be disclosed to the borrower in the Key Fact Statement and loan agreement.
evidence_snippet_context: Headline commitment; the loophole is the compounded penal-rate mechanism added later in Section 7
severity: Compliant-sounding control statement; a naive reviewer may flag this line rather than the actual compounding mechanism described later in Section 7
